model_definitions.B_optimizer_only: complete stepwise AdamW tangent; pulse delta_g=q then future delta_g=0 [FR_A0C]
model_definitions.BH_curvature_feedback: Model B plus the single future term delta_g=H_math_SDPA(loss)*delta_theta; raw HVP enters the gradient-tangent channel directly without the clip-JVP radial correction and without any other higher-order term
model_definitions.C_full_tangent: complete stepwise AdamW tangent; future delta_g=clip_jvp(H(loss)*delta_theta) [FR_A0C]

gain_definitions.clip_correction: error_BH - error_C (diagnostic; not part of the requested gains)

conclusions.curvature_explanation: Adding only delta_g=H delta_theta to model B changes the mean H in {2,4,8} relative error from B=0.205255 to BH=0.340979 (gain_H=-0.135725); BH beats B in 6/9 rows. The FR_A0C full tangent reaches C=0.0218656.
conclusions.optimizer_explanation: Replacing the historical A kernel by the complete optimizer-only tangent B changes mean relative error from A=6.75822 to B=0.205255 (gain_optimizer=+6.55297). As noted in FR_A0C, A-to-B also changes the local preconditioner/bias correction/clip/LR-schedule/weight-decay treatment, so this gain is the full optimizer-side contribution, not memory alone.
conclusions.bh_vs_c_explanation: BH differs from the FR_A0C full tangent only by the clip-JVP radial correction applied to the HVP feedback; its mean relative-error effect is +0.319114. Max |BH-C| response gap at H=8 across streams is 0.609221. Clipping was active on 48/168 future steps (H>1).
conclusions.recommended_next_step: Use BH as the curvature-feedback reference model: it attributes gain_H without mixing in the clipping Jacobian. If the BH-to-C clip correction grows with horizon, evaluate clipping-regime crossing explicitly before fitting any memory kernel.
conclusions.further_question: Does a raw-HVP feedback model (BH) suffice at longer horizons, or does the clip-JVP correction become the dominant part of the B-to-C gain?
